decision.detail: I cross the lobby floor—past the piano Phil is saving for eight, past the saucer Larry set down without putting back on the tray—and take the regional handset off the hook. The dial tone is already there, the line open, the patch patched through to Pittsburgh. I press the transmit key. Alma's voice runs out of the speaker and down the wire: forty-two winters of reel counters and lamp changes, and then, at the end, the part where she talks to her daughter. I let it finish. I do not cut it short. I let the silence after the last word sit on the line for three full seconds. Then I set the handset back.
decision.intention: Get Alma's voice to her daughter in Pittsburgh tonight, before the last reel ships and the Rialto's line goes dark with the building.
decision.words: —nothing to anyone. The line is the only audience that matters for this.

Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
